props.gloss_en: the first blast is to stop the people from work in the fields
the second is to stop the city and the shops
the third is to light the lamp (R' Natan)
the third is to remove tefillin (Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi)
he pauses as long as it takes to roast a small fish or to stick bread in the oven, then sounds tekia, terua, tekia, and rests
RSBG, as transmitted: the Babylonians sound a tekia and a terua and rest in the midst of the terua
emended: the Babylonians sound a tekia, sound again, and sound a terua, and rest in the midst of the terua
the custom of their fathers is in their hands
Rav Yehuda, as transmitted: the second blast is to light the lamp
the emended teaching (the third is to light the lamp) follows R' Natan
those near are not permitted to enter until those far away come, and they all enter as one
R' Yosei bar Chanina: I heard that one who comes to light after the six blasts may light
for the Sages gave the synagogue attendant a measure [of time] to carry his shofar to his house
rather, the synagogue attendant had a hidden place on top of his roof, where he put his shofar
since one may move neither the shofar nor the trumpets
a shofar may be moved, and trumpets may not be moved
just as one may move the shofar, so one may move the trumpets
Rav Yosef: no difficulty -- here [where the shofar is moved] it is an individual's, there [where it is not] the community's
this [a shofar is moved, trumpets not] is R' Yehuda
this [as a shofar is moved so are trumpets] is R' Shimon
this [neither shofar nor trumpets is moved] is R' Nechemya
and what is [meant by] 'shofar'? also trumpets

what practical difference does it make? for the shofar of Rosh HaShana
Rav Chisda: what was 'arava' (willow) is called 'tzaftzafa', and 'tzaftzafa' 'arava'
what practical difference does it make? for the lulav
